# ODF Suite

> ODF Suite is three zero-dependency JavaScript libraries that read OpenDocument files entirely in the browser: odt-engine for .odt text documents, ods-engine for .ods spreadsheets and odp-engine for .odp presentations. Each library is one self-contained ES module of 17-23 KB that is loaded from a URL or copied into a project as a single file. There is no install step, no build step and no server.

## Packages

- [odt-engine](https://github.com/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite/tree/main/packages/odt-engine): reads .odt headings, styled runs, links, lists, tables and images. Exports a JSON AST, print-ready HTML, Markdown and plain text.
- [ods-engine](https://github.com/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite/tree/main/packages/ods-engine): reads .ods typed cells, formulas, dates, booleans, percentages, merged cells and column widths. Exports a typed matrix, RFC 4180 CSV, header-keyed JSON and landscape print HTML.
- [odp-engine](https://github.com/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite/tree/main/packages/odp-engine): reads .odp slides, frame geometry, text, bullets, shapes, images and master backgrounds. Exports positioned slide HTML and a Markdown transcript.

## Quick facts

- Size: one file per library per build, two builds each. Module build: odt-engine 23.35 KB minified (8.97 KB gzipped), ods-engine 17.17 KB (7.05 KB), odp-engine 18.78 KB (7.69 KB). Script-tag build: 23.82 KB, 17.64 KB, 19.25 KB.
- Runtime dependencies: none. Every library has an empty dependencies map.
- Input: File, Blob, ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array. Output: HTML with CSS Paged Media, Markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON and a JSON AST.
- Delivery: jsDelivr and GitHub Pages serve the same bytes, pinned to the v1.0.0 releases; copying one library into a project is a single curl command.
- Browser parse benchmark: about 5 MB of XML in headless Chrome 155, median of seven timed runs after warm-up. ODT 122-128 ms, ODS 194-195 ms, ODP 196-201 ms. Most of the time is the browser's own XML parser (62 ms for ODT, 112-121 ms for ODS and ODP) plus 13-15 ms of decompression.
- Memory: 40 parse, render and destroy cycles over an 18 KB document with 120 images move the retained heap by less than 1 MB, with image Blob URLs revoked every cycle.
- Verification: 116 Node tests and 15 browser checks, including five documents written by LibreOffice, StarOffice and OpenOffice.org.
- Browser support: Chrome 80+, Edge 80+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.4+, or any runtime with DecompressionStream, DOMParser and Blob URLs.
- Not published to npm. Distribution is a URL import or a single-file download.
- License: MIT.

## Load a library

Install nothing. Each library ships two builds: dist/global.js for a plain script tag (defines window.ODT, window.ODS or window.ODP) and dist/index.js for import.

Script tag, anywhere in the page or in the head:

    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite@odt-engine-v1.0.0/packages/odt-engine/dist/global.js"></script>
    <script>
      ODT.parseODT(file).then((doc) => {
        document.querySelector('#preview').innerHTML = doc.toHTML();
      });
    </script>

ES module import:

    import { parseODT } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite@odt-engine-v1.0.0/packages/odt-engine/dist/index.js';

or a module script in a page head (type="module" is required; module scripts are deferred, so the DOM is ready):

    <head>
      <script type="module">
        import { parseODT } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite@odt-engine-v1.0.0/packages/odt-engine/dist/index.js';

        const input = document.querySelector('input[type=file]');
        input.addEventListener('change', async () => {
          const doc = await parseODT(input.files[0]);
          document.querySelector('#preview').innerHTML = doc.toHTML();
        });
      </script>
    </head>

GitHub Pages serves the same files:

- odt-engine: https://spuds0588.github.io/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite/packages/odt-engine/dist/global.js and .../dist/index.js
- ods-engine: https://spuds0588.github.io/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite/packages/ods-engine/dist/global.js and .../dist/index.js
- odp-engine: https://spuds0588.github.io/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite/packages/odp-engine/dist/global.js and .../dist/index.js

Replace the release tag with `main` to follow the newest build. To survive one host being unavailable, try the URLs in order with `await import(url)` and a `try/catch`.

## Copy one library into a project

One command downloads the complete library. Use global.js for a script tag, index.js for import:

    curl -sLo odt-engine.js https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Spuds0588/OpenDocument-Engine-Suite@odt-engine-v1.0.0/packages/odt-engine/dist/global.js

    <script src="./odt-engine.js"></script>

    import { parseODT } from './odt-engine.js';

Swap odt-engine for ods-engine or odp-engine in the command. Nothing else has to be downloaded, installed or kept in sync; TypeScript declarations are at dist/index.d.ts next to each module bundle.

## Usage

    import { parseODT } from './odt-engine.js';

    const doc = await parseODT(file);
    document.querySelector('#preview').innerHTML = doc.toHTML();
    console.log(doc.toMarkdown());
    doc.destroy();

Spreadsheets use parseODS and expose toMatrix, toCSV, toJSON and toHTML. Presentations use parseODP and expose toHTML and toMarkdown. Call destroy() to revoke Blob URLs created for embedded images. Printing to PDF uses the browser: toHTML() returns a complete document with CSS Paged Media rules, and triggerPrintToPDF(html) opens the print dialog in an off-screen iframe.

## Limitations

- Read-only; no editing.
- OpenDocument only; no DOCX, XLSX, PPTX or legacy binary formats.
- ZIP64 archives are rejected and encrypted entries are skipped.
- ODT footnotes and comments are not in the AST.
- Spreadsheet formulas are preserved but not evaluated.
- Slide animation and media are not rendered.
- Built for documents in the low-megabyte range; repeat counters are clipped to predictable limits.
